utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Welcome back. Today we build the foundation of the whole course: the supply and demand model.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Demand is the quantity of a good that buyers are willing and able to purchase at a given price.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: For example, when the price of coffee went from three dollars to five dollars at the campus cafe, daily sales dropped by almost half.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: The law of demand is the principle that, all else equal, quantity demanded falls as price rises.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Supply is the quantity of a good that producers are willing to sell at a given price.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: For example, when coffee prices rose, two new roasters entered the market because selling coffee became more profitable.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Equilibrium is the price at which the quantity buyers want exactly equals the quantity sellers offer.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: A shortage is the situation where quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: For instance, during the shortage last spring, the bookstore ran out of calculators in the first week.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: A surplus is the situation where quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the current price.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Elasticity is a measure of how strongly quantity demanded or supplied responds to a change in price.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: For example, demand for insulin is nearly unchanging when its price rises, while demand for concert tickets falls quickly.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Now the commitments, write these down. Your first exam is on Thursday, October 29, and it covers everything through elasticity.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: Problem set 3 is due Friday at the start of class.

utterances.speaker: Professor Alvarez
utterances.text: And read chapter 4 before Monday's class, because we start market failures then.
